name: LDC1312QDNTRQ1
title: LDC1312-Q1 / LDC1314-Q1 automotive 2- and 4-channel 12-bit inductance-to-digital converters
summary: The LDC1312-Q1 (two channels, WSON-12) and LDC1314-Q1 (four channels, WQFN-16) drive external L-C resonators and report each tank's oscillation frequency as a 12-bit ratio to a reference clock, so a conductive target moving near a coil shows up as a code change. Sensor frequencies from 1 kHz to 10 MHz are accepted, the reference comes from a 2-40 MHz CLKIN or an internal oscillator, and results and setup go over I2C at up to 400 kHz. The parts run from 2.7-3.6 V, draw 35 µA asleep and 0.2 µA in shutdown, and are AEC-Q100 Grade 1 qualified for -40 °C to 125 °C.
key_figures: 12 bits (up to 16 effective bits with output gain)
1 kΩ to 100 kΩ (250 Ω min on channel 0 in high-current drive)

circuits.title: Example multi-channel application, LDC1312
circuits.description: Two L-C tank sensors, each a coil with a capacitor across it, hang between IN0A/IN0B and IN1A/IN1B; a conductive target moves along each coil's axis. A 40 MHz clock feeds CLKIN as the reference. A host MCU on the same 3.3 V rail reads results over I2C (SDA, SCL), drives SD from one GPIO and watches INTB on another. ADDR is tied to 3.3 V, so the address is 0x2B. In the worked design channel 0 measures proximity with a 43.9 µH, 100 pF tank (2.4 MHz, RP = 6.6 kΩ) and channel 1 can carry a reference coil for temperature compensation.

parts.note: sensor 0 PCB coil: 2 layers, 39 turns, 1.77 cm diameter

notes: The supply wants a 1 µF X7R ceramic from VDD to GND, as close to the pins as possible; a supply more than a few inches away may also need about 10 µF of bulk electrolytic.
The die-attach pad joins GND.

operation.text: An AC current in the sensor coil sets up a field that induces eddy currents in a nearby conductive target; their own field opposes the coil's, and the tank sees this as a shift in inductance and so in resonant frequency. Each front end keeps its tank oscillating; a multiplexer steps through the active channels and connects each to a core that measures the tank frequency against fREF. The result is proportional to fSENSOR/fREF and can be converted to an equivalent inductance. The coupling behaves like a secondary winding whose resistance and inductance depend on the target's distance, size, shape and resistivity, and appear on the coil side as RP(d) and L(d).

fCLK is either the internal oscillator (about 43.4 MHz) or CLKIN (2-40 MHz), chosen by CONFIG.REF_CLK_SRC. Each channel divides fCLK by CHx_FREF_DIVIDER to get fREFx and divides its sensor frequency by CHx_FIN_DIVIDER to get fINx; fINx must stay below fREFx/4. An external clock is recommended where precision matters; the internal oscillator suits low-cost designs without it. With the internal oscillator, CLKIN is grounded.

With MUX_CONFIG.AUTOSCAN_EN = 0 the part converts one channel, picked by CONFIG.ACTIVE_CHAN, continuously. With AUTOSCAN_EN = 1 it converts each channel of the RR_SEQUENCE set in turn (Ch0-Ch1, Ch0-Ch2 or Ch0-Ch3). A second sensor can serve as a reference that cancels a temperature shift in the resonant frequency. In sequence, each channel's dwell is its sensor activation (settling) time, its conversion time and the switch delay. In single-channel mode, an amplitude correction runs between conversions.

The core measures to 16 bits and the DATA registers carry 12. When a signal spans less than 25% of full scale, RESET_DEV.OUTPUT_GAIN shifts the result left by 2, 3 or 4 bits (gain 4, 8 or 16) on all channels, exposing the lower bits and discarding the top ones. Gain is not to be used while any active channel's top bits change. Example: a result of 0x07A3 reads 0x07A at gain 1 and 0x7A3 at gain 16.

Normal drive is up to 1.5 mA per channel. With CONFIG.HIGH_CURRENT_DRV = 1, channel 0 alone, in single-channel mode only, can be driven above 1.5 mA, for sensors with RP below 1 kΩ. For normal operation set RP_OVERRIDE_EN = 1, AUTO_AMP_DIS = 1 and SENSOR_ACTIVATE_SEL = 0 (full-current activation), and program CHx_IDRIVE from the RP table using RP at the largest target distance. Automatic amplitude correction holds the oscillation between 1.2 V and 1.8 V by trimming drive between conversions, but can make the output non-monotonic; it suits low-precision use only. Auto-calibration finds a drive level for a fixed sensor design and is meant for prototyping. Drive that pushes the amplitude above 1.8 V turns on the internal ESD clamps and shifts the frequency; too little drive lowers SNR and, with the target very close, oscillation can stop and the results read all zero.

Use when RP is unknown, in prototyping or at start-up: put the target at its farthest operating distance; enter sleep mode; program SETTLECOUNT and RCOUNT; clear RP_OVERRIDE_EN to enable auto-calibration; leave sleep mode; let at least one measurement complete with the target held still; read CHx_INIT_IDRIVE (DRIVE_CURRENT_CHx bits 10:6) and store it. At each normal start-up, write the stored value into CHx_IDRIVE (bits 15:11) and set RP_OVERRIDE_EN = 1 to fix the drive.

INTB reports a STATUS event when the event is unmasked in ERROR_CONFIG and CONFIG.INTB_DIS = 0. Once a STATUS bit sets, the whole register holds until STATUS or the DATA register is read; the read also releases INTB. Interrupts also clear on entering sleep, power-on reset, shutdown (SD high) and software reset. INTB_DIS = 1 keeps INTB high. A data-ready flag (DRDY) supports interrupt-driven reading; otherwise the fixed conversion time allows polling at a set interval.

A filter on the sensor inputs rejects EMI and ringing above the sensor frequency without affecting the result, provided its bandwidth exceeds the highest sensor frequency. Choose the lowest MUX_CONFIG.DEGLITCH setting above it: for a 2.0 MHz sensor, b100 (3.3 MHz).

At power-up the part enters sleep mode and waits to be configured; setting CONFIG.SLEEP_MODE_EN to 0 starts conversions. Configuration is done in sleep; to change a setting, return to sleep, write, and leave sleep again. In sleep the registers keep their values and I2C works, but nothing converts; entering sleep clears results and errors and releases INTB. After SLEEP_MODE_EN goes to 0, the first sensor activation starts 16,384 fINT cycles later.

SD high puts the part in shutdown, its lowest-power state; SD low brings it out (wake-up to I2C readback within 2 ms). Shutdown returns every register to its default, clears errors and releases INTB, and I2C is not available during it. Writing RESET_DEV.RESET_DEV = 1 stops any conversion and restores all register defaults.

Registers are 16 bits, accessed with a 7-bit address followed by an 8-bit register pointer, at up to 400 kbit/s. A write sends address, pointer, then data MSB and LSB bytes, each acknowledged by the device. A read sends address and pointer, then a repeated start with the address, after which the device returns the MSB (acknowledged by the master) and the LSB (not acknowledged), and the master stops. ADDR low gives 0x2A, high gives 0x2B.

RP rises with target distance and depends on target material and the sensor; at resonance only RP loads the tank, and a lower RP needs more drive for the same amplitude. Drive must still sustain oscillation at the smallest RP, i.e. the nearest target: for the 14 mm coil with a stainless steel target, 1 mm gives about 5 kΩ. Without magnetic materials (ferrous metals, ferrites) the inductance shift depends only on current-flow geometry; temperature drift comes mostly from thermal expansion of the coil and mechanics, plus the drift of the tank capacitor.

Requirements: sensor 0 for proximity, sensor 1 for temperature compensation; target distance 0.1 cm, resolution 0.2 µm, target 1 cm diameter stainless steel (SS416); 2-layer coil; 500 SPS (TSAMPLE = 2000 µs). The resulting coil is 2 layers, 2.5 cm², 1.77 cm diameter, 39 turns, with RP = 6.6 kΩ, L = 43.9 µH, C = 100 pF, so fSENSOR = 2.4 MHz. With 40 MHz on CLKIN: CH0_FIN_DIVIDER = 1 (fSENSOR below 8.75 MHz) and CH0_FREF_DIVIDER = 2 for fREF0 = 20 MHz (more than 4 × fSENSOR), register 0x14 = 0x1002. Q = 10 gives a least settle count of 5.2, rounded to 6; 10 is used for margin, a settle time of 8 µs (0x10 = 0x000A). The switch delay is about 1 µs at 20 MHz. The conversion budget is 1000 − 8 − 1 = 991 µs, so CH0_RCOUNT = 1238 (0x04D6). ERROR_CONFIG stays at default (no interrupts). RP = 6.6 kΩ gives CH0_IDRIVE = 18, so DRIVE_CURRENT_CH0 = 0x9000. MUX_CONFIG = 0x820C (sequence Ch0, Ch1, deglitch 3.3 MHz). CONFIG = 0x1601 (channel 0, awake, RP override on, full-current activation, amplitude correction off, external clock), written last. Channel 1 takes the same settings; both results are read every 1000 µs.

Supply 2.7-3.6 V. Place a 1 µF X7R multilayer ceramic between VDD and GND as close to the pins as possible with the smallest loop; add bulk capacitance, typically a 10 µF electrolytic, when the supply is more than a few inches away.

Keep the traces from the LDC to the sensor short: long traces add parasitic capacitance to the sensor and reduce performance. The evaluation module uses four layers: signal on top, ground on the first inner layer, power on the second, signal on the bottom. The exposed pad is soldered to the board.
